key_insight: DiffVortex compresses the Biot–Savart kernel rather than the flow state, combining tensor-network acceleration with flexible Lagrangian vortex simulation.
engineering_relevance: Its differentiable GPU implementation supports incompressible-flow simulation around moving and deforming bodies, with potential for gradient-based design.
method: Evolve vorticity as Lagrangian particles and model immersed bodies with bound vortex sheets.
Use quantics tensor cross interpolation to precompute tensor-network contractions for fast-multipole moment-to-local interactions.
Prove that kernel QTT rank r yields convolution-operator MPO rank at most 2^d r, independent of grid resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 6.7×10^7 particles on one GPU, validation against cylinder and elliptical-vortex benchmarks, and gradients through full time integration.
watch_item: Efficiency depends on manageable tensor ranks; the resolution-independent rank bound does not guarantee low ranks for every kernel or configuration.
paper_title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
